minutes.headline: Committee declined to weigh in on the track article, kept the senior center network project, and set meetings for Nov 19 and Nov 30.
minutes.summary: The Capital Planning Committee reviewed its charter duties, then discussed whether to weigh in on the school's Article 9 track and field engineering request for the Nov 17 special town meeting. It concluded it would not make a recommendation because the item had not gone through its process, though capital projects should come through it. It then voted on keeping the Adult Activity Center network upgrade in the FY27 plan after its quote fell below the capital threshold, and scheduled department presentations.

votes.motion: Keep the Adult Activity Center network upgrade in the FY27 capital program and instruct IT to provide far more accurate quotes in future.

budget_items.what_was_said: The school's engineering and design study request is a step before a much larger construction project that the committee heard last year.

decisions.decision: The committee will make no recommendation on Article 9 since it did not go through its process, but advises all capital projects come through it.
Tentative meeting Nov 19 for police and fire; Monday Nov 30 at 6:30 and Dec 7 at 6:30 for DPW, school and facilities.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee voted 4-1 to keep the Adult Activity Center network upgrade in the FY27 capital program and told IT to give far more accurate quotes in future.
The committee will make no recommendation on the school's Article 9 track and field engineering request, saying it did not go through the committee's process.
The committee advised that all capital projects should come through it.
The network upgrade had been planned just over the capital threshold and came in under it after a vendor quote.
A tentative Nov 19 meeting was set for police and fire, with Nov 30 and Dec 7 at 6:30 for DPW, school and facilities.

why_it_matters: Article 9 goes to the Nov 17 special town meeting without a recommendation from the committee that reviews capital projects, so voters will decide it without that review.
The upcoming department presentations are where requests for the FY27 capital plan, which draws on the town budget, mostly taxes, will be heard.
